issues.claim: where gravity is weaker, so their clocks run fast
issues.problem: Weaker gravity gives +45 µs/day; orbital speed subtracts ~7 µs/day. Line 4 says 'net' so it's consistent, but line 3 alone implies gravity is the whole story.
issues.fix: Satellites orbit 20,000 kilometres up, where gravity is weaker, so their clocks gain time, even after speed slows them a bit.

issues.claim: about ten kilometres off every day
issues.problem: Ohio State says ~10 km/day; Wikipedia says ~11.4 km/day. 'About ten' is acceptable; errors accumulate rather than being a fixed offset.
issues.fix: Without Einstein, your phone's GPS would drift about ten kilometres further off every day.
